77998.e: Travel, a book and good tips make a travel guide. It describes the sights at a holiday destination.
77998.m: A travel guide gives tips for your destination.

77999.q: Which famous Swiss train do these pictures mean?
77999.e: A glacier, a train and mountains show the Glacier Express. It runs from Zermatt to St Moritz and is said to be the slowest express train in the world.
77999.m: The Glacier Express runs from Zermatt to St Moritz.

78000.q: What kind of journey do these pictures show?
78000.e: A big ship, the sea and islands show a cruise. You travel on a ship and visit several places.
78000.m: On a cruise, you live on a ship.

78001.q: Which travel problem do these pictures mean?
78001.e: Flying, a different time and tiredness show jet lag. It happens when you fly quickly across several time zones.
78001.m: Jet lag comes from flights across time zones.

78002.q: Which means of transport do these pictures make together?
78002.e: Cable, car and mountain make cable car. The cabin hangs from cables and travels up the mountain.
78002.m: On a cable car, the cabin hangs from cables.

78003.q: Which holiday activity do these pictures show?
78003.e: Hiking boots, a mountain and a map show hiking. Switzerland has a dense network of footpaths marked in yellow.
78003.m: Swiss footpaths are marked in yellow.

78004.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
78004.e: Air and bed (mattress) make airbed. You can lie on it by the water or sleep on it in a tent.
78004.m: An airbed is filled with air.

78005.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
78005.e: Sun and umbrella make sun umbrella. It gives shade on the beach or in the garden.

78006.q: What kind of holiday do these pictures show?
78006.e: A tent, a campfire and a forest show a camp. The Scouts, for example, often go to camp in summer.
78006.m: At camp, you sleep in a tent.

78008.q: Which feeling on holiday do these pictures mean?
78008.e: A house, a thought and sadness show homesickness. You miss your home, for example at camp.
78008.m: Homesickness means you miss your home.

78009.e: A postbox, a picture and the beach show the picture postcard. It shows a picture of the holiday place and is sent by post.
78009.m: People like to send a postcard from their holidays.

78010.q: Which holiday problem do these pictures mean?
78010.e: Lots of cars and a snail show the traffic jam. At the start of the holidays, there are often traffic jams in front of the Gotthard road tunnel.
78010.m: At the start of the holidays, there are often traffic jams at the Gotthard.

78011.q: Which festival do these pictures mean?
78011.e: A pumpkin, sweets and a ghost show Halloween. It is celebrated on 31 October.

78012.q: Which festival do these pictures mean?
78012.e: Masks, drums, trumpets and confetti show carnival (Fasnacht). The Basel carnival has been part of UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage since 2017.

78013.q: Which public holiday do these pictures mean?
78013.e: The numbers 1 and 8, fireworks and paper lanterns show Swiss National Day on 1 August. It is the national holiday of Switzerland.
78013.m: Switzerland's national holiday is on 1 August.

78014.q: Which Zurich festival do these pictures mean?
78014.e: A snowman in the fire, horses and six o'clock show Sechseläuten. At 6 p.m., the Böögg is set alight, and riders circle the fire.
78014.m: At Sechseläuten, the Böögg is burnt.

78015.q: Which market in Bern do these pictures mean?
78015.e: Onions, shopping and the bear for Bern show the Zibelemärit, the onion market. It takes place every year on the fourth Monday in November.
78015.m: The Zibelemärit is an onion market in Bern.

78016.q: Which Swiss custom do these pictures mean?
78016.e: Decorated cows with bells coming down the mountain show the Alpine descent. In autumn, the animals come back from the Alpine pastures to the valley.
78016.m: In the Alpine descent, the cows return to the valley in autumn.

78017.q: Who comes on 6 December with these pictures?
78017.e: A man with a beard, mandarins and nuts show the Samichlaus, the Swiss St Nicholas. He comes on 6 December, often together with Schmutzli.

78018.q: Which festival do these pictures mean?
78018.e: A big wheel, a merry-go-round and sweets show the Chilbi. That is what a funfair is called in Switzerland.
78018.m: A Chilbi is a funfair with rides.

78019.q: Which time of the church year do these pictures mean?
78019.e: Fir branches, candles and the number four show Advent. The Advent wreath has four candles for the four Sundays before Christmas.
78019.m: Four candles burn on the Advent wreath.

78021.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
78021.e: Hearing (ear) and book make audiobook. A book is read aloud and you listen.
78021.m: You listen to an audiobook instead of reading it.

78022.q: Which place do these pictures mean?
78022.e: A clapperboard, popcorn and a ticket show the cinema. There you watch films on a big screen.
78022.m: At the cinema, you watch films on a screen.

78023.q: What kind of photo do these pictures mean?
78023.e: If you point your mobile at yourself, you take a selfie. A selfie is a photo you take of yourself.
78023.m: A selfie is a photo of yourself.

78024.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
78024.e: Computer and game (controller) make computer game. With games, you should pay attention to the recommended age.
78024.m: With computer games, you check the age rating.

78025.q: What kind of film do these pictures mean?
78025.e: A pencil, a film strip and a mouse show the cartoon. Lots of drawn pictures are shown quickly one after another.
78025.m: A cartoon is made of lots of drawn pictures.

78026.q: What kind of film do these pictures mean?
78026.e: No sound, a film strip and a hat like Charlie Chaplin's show the silent film. Until the end of the 1920s, films mostly had no spoken sound.
78026.m: Silent films have no spoken sound.

78027.q: Which programme do these pictures mean?
78027.e: Sun and clouds, a television and a map show the weather forecast. It predicts the weather for the next few days.
78027.m: The weather forecast predicts the weather.

78098.q: Which saying with a colour does this picture puzzle show?
78098.e: Among several sheep, a black one stands out. “The black sheep” is someone who stands out in a group in a bad way.
78098.m: The black sheep of a family stands out because of bad behaviour.

78204.q: Which Bible story do these emojis show?
78204.e: A big ship, animals in pairs, rain, a dove and a rainbow: Noah saves his family and the animals from the Flood.
78204.m: After the Flood, Noah sent out a dove, which came back with an olive branch.

78346.q: Which animal behaviour do these pictures mean?
78346.e: In autumn, birds fly to warmer parts of the world. This behaviour is called bird migration; swallows from Switzerland, for example, spend the winter in Africa.
78346.m: Migratory birds spend the winter in warmer regions.

78393.e: A dinosaur in rock stands for a fossil. Fossils are the remains or traces of living things from earlier ages of the Earth, turned to stone.
78393.m: Fossils are evidence of life from prehistoric times.

78405.q: Which form of energy do these pictures mean?
78405.e: Wind turns a wheel, and this makes electricity. Wind turbines turn the movement energy of the air into electrical energy.
78405.m: Wind turbines use the movement energy of the air.

78428.q: Which country do these emojis show?
78428.e: The maple leaf is on Canada's flag, the beaver is an official national symbol and ice hockey is the national winter sport. Together, that makes Canada.
78428.m: Canada is the second largest country on Earth by area.

78429.q: Which country do these pictures mean?
78429.e: Koalas live in the wild only in Australia, and almost all kangaroos live there too. The dry outback covers large parts of the country.
78429.m: Australia is both a country and a whole continent.

78430.q: Which country do these emojis show?
78430.e: Tacos, cacti and the colourful piñata are seen as typical of Mexico. Maize for tortillas was grown there thousands of years ago.
78430.m: Mexico is the Spanish-speaking country with the most people in the world.

78431.e: The picture shows Mount Fuji, the highest mountain in Japan, along with sushi and the Shinkansen high-speed train, which has been running since 1964.
78431.m: Mount Fuji is a volcano and, at 3776 metres, the highest mountain in Japan.

78432.q: Which country do these emojis show?
78432.e: The giant panda lives in the wild only in China; chopsticks and red lanterns, for example at the Lantern Festival, are part of Chinese culture.
78432.m: China is one of the countries with the most people on Earth.

78433.q: Which country do these pictures mean?
78433.e: Elephants, curries and yoga, which has its origins in India, together point to India.

78434.q: Which country do these pictures mean?
78434.e: Camels in the desert, the pyramids and the crocodiles in the Nile point to Egypt.
78434.m: Egypt lies in north-east Africa on the Nile.

78437.q: Which city do these emojis mean?
78437.e: The bear is on the coat of arms of Bern, the Federal Palace is the seat of the Federal Council and Parliament, and in clear weather you can see the Alps. Bern is the federal city of Switzerland.
78437.m: Officially, Switzerland has no capital; Bern is the federal city.

78438.q: Which capital do these pictures show?
78438.e: The gate stands for the Brandenburg Gate, the bear for the city's coat of arms and the wall for the Berlin Wall, which divided the city from 1961 to 1989.
78438.m: The Wall divided Berlin into East and West for 28 years.

78440.q: Which capital do these emojis show?
78440.e: The stadium stands for the Colosseum, the fountain for the Trevi Fountain, pasta and scooters for Italian city life. Together that makes the Italian capital.
78440.m: The Colosseum is the largest amphitheatre of the ancient world.

78441.e: The guards outside Buckingham Palace, the red double-decker buses and the frequent rain are seen as typical of London.
78441.m: London lies on the Thames and is the capital of the United Kingdom.

78445.q: Which landmark do these emojis show?
78445.e: The statue holds a torch and a tablet with the date of the Declaration of Independence. France gave it to the USA, and it was unveiled in New York in 1886.
78445.m: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France to the USA.

78471.q: Which form of trade do these emojis show?
78471.e: The arrows in a circle show that a cow is swapped directly for grain, without any money at all.
78471.m: In barter, goods are swapped for each other without money.

78473.e: The goods leave your own country and go out into the world. Selling goods abroad is called exporting.
78473.m: Exports are goods that are sold abroad.

78511.e: The ticket divided by two makes half the price. With the Half Fare Travelcard, you travel on Swiss public transport at half price.
78511.m: With the Half Fare Travelcard, you pay only half price on public transport.

78515.e: Red plus sea makes the Red Sea between Africa and the Arabian Peninsula, which is known for its colourful coral reefs and fish.
78515.m: The Red Sea is famous for its coral reefs.

78517.q: Which sea do these emojis show?
78517.e: Olives, lemons and lots of sun typically grow and thrive around the Mediterranean Sea, which separates Europe, Africa and Asia.
78517.m: Around the Mediterranean, there is a warm climate with dry summers.

78519.q: Which natural phenomenon do these emojis show?
78519.e: The pull of the Moon makes the sea level rise and fall regularly. This change between low tide and high tide is called the tides.
78519.m: Low and high tide are caused mainly by the pull of the Moon.

78520.q: Which climate zone do these emojis show?
78520.e: Palm trees, lots of rain and high temperatures all year round mark the tropics around the equator.
78520.m: In the tropics it is warm all year round.

78521.e: Penguins, snow and the polar night lasting for months mark the coldest areas of the Earth at the poles.
78521.m: In the polar zone, there is the polar night in winter.

78525.q: Which climate zone do these pictures mean?
78525.e: Autumn, spring, summer and winter show the four clear seasons. They mark the temperate zone, where Switzerland lies too.
78525.m: Switzerland lies in the temperate climate zone.

78527.q: Which vegetation zone do these emojis show?
78527.e: Sand, dromedaries, cacti and strong sun mark the desert. So little rain falls there that hardly any plants grow.
78527.m: Very little rain falls in the desert.

78573.q: Which technology do these emojis show?
78573.e: The computer receives a radio signal and needs no network cable. A wireless local network is called Wi-Fi or WLAN (Wireless Local Area Network).
78573.m: Wi-Fi connects devices to the network without cables.

78585.q: Which kind of picture do these emojis show?
78585.e: A painter looks in the mirror and paints himself. A picture like this is called a self-portrait; those by Rembrandt, for example, are famous.
78585.m: In a self-portrait, artists show themselves.

78588.q: Which art technique do these emojis mean?
78588.e: Lots of small coloured squares together make a picture. In a mosaic, you put small stones or pieces of glass together to make a picture.
78588.m: A mosaic is made of lots of small coloured stones.

78589.q: Which painting technique goes with these emojis?
78589.e: Painting is done on paper with water, a brush and paint. Painting with see-through water-based paints is called watercolour (in German “Aquarell”, from Latin aqua, water).
78589.m: A watercolour is painted with water-based paints.

78606.q: Which running event do these pictures mean?
78606.e: The number 42 stands for the distance of 42.195 kilometres. This long-distance race is called a marathon, named after the Greek town of Marathon.

78607.q: Which sport do these emojis show?
78607.e: Swimming, cycling and running are done straight after each other. This endurance sport is called triathlon (Greek tri, three).
78607.m: The triathlon is made up of swimming, cycling and running.

78609.e: A ball lies about 11 metres in front of the goal, and only the goalkeeper may try to stop it. This kick is called a penalty.
78609.m: A penalty is taken from the penalty spot.

78622.q: Which job with a French name goes with these emojis?
78622.e: A person with a cap drives other people in a car. Someone who drives a vehicle as a job is called a chauffeur.
78622.m: A chauffeur drives other people in a car.

78623.q: Which job with a French name is meant?
78623.e: Hair is cut with scissors, and the striped sign stands for a salon. In Switzerland, a hairdresser is called a coiffeur.
78623.m: The coiffeur cuts and styles hair.

78631.q: Which painting do these emojis mean?
78631.e: Leonardo da Vinci painted the woman with the mysterious smile in front of a wide landscape; the picture hangs today in the Louvre in Paris.
78631.m: The Mona Lisa's smile is seen as the most famous in the history of art.

78764.q: Which term from psychology do these pictures mean?
78764.e: Sun and a thought bubble with a sleepy face make day and dream. In a daydream, your thoughts wander while you are awake.
78764.m: In a daydream, your thoughts wander even though you are awake.

78778.q: Which term from the digital world do these pictures mean?
78778.e: A screen (mobile and computer) is photographed. A photo of the screen is called a screenshot.
78778.m: With a screenshot, you save a picture of the screen.

78790.q: Which term from linguistics do these pictures mean?
78790.e: Hands and hand signs replace the spoken word. Deaf people communicate with sign language; in Switzerland there are three sign languages.
78790.m: Sign languages are full languages that work with the hands, the face and the body.

79318.q: Why are pebbles from a stream usually round and smooth?
a: The water has rolled them for a long time
79318.e: The water rolls the stones back and forth in the stream for a long time. This wears the corners away, and the stones become round and smooth.
79318.m: Pebbles are worn round by the water.

79319.q: Where can you find lots of pebbles?
a: On the bank of a river
79319.e: Rivers and streams carry stones along and leave them on the bank. That is why there are lots of pebbles there.
79319.m: There are lots of pebbles on a riverbank.

79320.q: What do you call throwing flat stones across a lake so that they bounce several times?
79320.e: If you throw a flat pebble low across the water, it bounces several times. Some people also call it skipping stones.
79320.m: A flat pebble can bounce across the water.

79321.q: Which shape is best for making a stone bounce across the water?
79321.e: A flat, round stone glides well over the surface of the water. That is why it bounces more often than a ball-shaped stone.
79321.m: Flat, round stones bounce best across the water.

79322.q: Where do the pebbles in Swiss rivers originally come from?
79322.e: In the mountains, stones break off rocks. Streams and rivers carry them down the valley, and on the way they become round.
79322.m: Many pebbles originally come from the mountains.

79323.q: What do you call lots of small pebbles together, for example on a garden path?
79323.e: Gravel is made of lots of small, roundish stones. It is used for paths, squares and in building.
79323.m: Gravel is made of lots of small stones.

79324.q: What is the rock on the Rigi called, in which lots of round pebbles are baked together?
79324.e: Nagelfluh is made of many round pebbles that are firmly cemented together. You can find it on the Rigi and the Rossberg, for example.
79324.m: Nagelfluh is full of round pebbles.

79325.q: Why do pebbles often look shinier when they are wet?
a: The water makes the colours glow
Wet stones are made of glass
79325.e: A thin layer of water makes the surface smooth. This lets you see the colours and patterns of the stones better.
79325.m: Wet pebbles show their colours better.

79326.q: What does granite usually look like?
79326.e: Granite is made of many small grains in different colours. That is why it looks speckled.

79327.q: Is granite a hard or a soft stone?
a: A stone as soft as chalk
79327.e: Granite is very hard and tough. That is why it is used for stairs, fountains and kitchen worktops.
79327.m: Granite is a very hard stone.

a: From hot, liquid rock deep inside the Earth
From sand pressed together on the beach
79328.e: Granite was formed from red-hot, liquid rock. It cooled slowly deep inside the Earth and became hard.
79328.m: Granite formed from liquid rock that cooled down.

79329.q: What often glitters in a piece of granite?
79329.e: Granite contains mica. These are thin flakes that glitter in the light.

79330.q: What is granite often used for?
79330.e: Granite is hard and hardly wears away. That is why streets and squares are paved with it.
79330.m: Paving stones are made from granite.

79331.q: In which part of Switzerland is there a lot of granite?
79331.e: In the Alps, for example at the Grimsel and the Gotthard, there is a lot of granite. You can see huge grey rock faces there.
79331.m: There is a lot of granite in the Swiss Alps.

79332.q: What is the most common colour of granite?
79332.e: Many granites are grey with light and dark dots. But there is also reddish granite.

79333.q: What does the German saying “auf Granit beissen” (to bite on granite) mean?
79333.e: Granite is so hard that you cannot bite into it. If you “bite on granite”, you do not get what you want, a bit like hitting a brick wall.
79333.m: If you bite on granite, you get nowhere.

79334.q: What did a lot of limestone form from?
a: From the shells of sea creatures
79334.e: Long ago, many animals with shells lived in the sea. Their shells sank to the seabed and turned into limestone.
79334.m: A lot of limestone formed from the shells of sea creatures.

79335.q: Which mountain range in north-west Switzerland is largely made of limestone?
79335.e: The Jura is a mountain range made of limestone. You often find fossilised shells from an ancient sea in it.
79335.m: The Jura is largely made of limestone.

79336.q: What happens if you drip vinegar onto limestone?
79336.e: Vinegar is an acid. It dissolves limestone, and this makes tiny bubbles that foam.

79337.q: What are caves with spikes of limestone hanging from the ceiling called?
79337.e: Water dissolves limestone and drips from the cave ceiling. It leaves limestone behind, and slowly dripstones grow.
79337.m: Spikes of limestone grow in dripstone caves.

79338.q: What kind of stone is natural chalk?
79338.e: Natural chalk is a soft, white limestone. It is made of tiny shells of sea creatures.
79338.m: Natural chalk is a soft limestone.

79339.e: Limestone is usually light coloured, often grey, whitish or yellowish. That is why limestone cliffs shine brightly in the sun.

79340.q: What is the huge cave in the Muota valley in the canton of Schwyz called?
79340.e: The Hölloch is in the Muota valley in the canton of Schwyz. It is one of the longest caves in the world and lies in limestone.
79340.m: The Hölloch is a huge cave in limestone.

79341.q: Which white coating builds up inside a kettle over time?
79341.e: Tap water contains dissolved lime. When the water boils, it is left behind as a white coating in the kettle.
79341.m: Limescale builds up in a kettle over time.

79342.q: What are the limestone spikes called that grow down from the ceiling of a cave?
79342.e: Stalactites hang down from the ceiling. The dripstones that grow up from the floor are called stalagmites.
79342.m: Stalactites hang from the cave ceiling.

79343.e: Sandstone is made of lots of grains of sand. Over a long time they were pressed and cemented together.
79343.m: Sandstone is made of grains of sand stuck together.

79344.q: Which stone is much of Bern's old town built from?
79344.e: Many houses, the arcades and the Minster in Bern are built of sandstone. Bernese sandstone is greenish grey.
79344.m: Bern's old town is built of sandstone.

79345.q: What happens if you rub your finger hard over old sandstone?
79345.e: Sandstone is not as solid as granite. If you rub it, single grains of sand often come loose.
79345.m: Grains of sand come off sandstone easily.

79346.q: Why did sculptors like working with sandstone?
79346.e: Sandstone is softer than many other stones. That is why it can easily be shaped with a chisel and hammer.

79347.q: Which famous red rock in Australia is made of sandstone?
79347.e: Uluru is a huge rock in the middle of Australia. It is made of sandstone and glows red at sunset.
79347.m: Uluru in Australia is made of sandstone.

79348.q: What wears sandstone down over time so that it crumbles?
79348.e: Rain, frost and wind gradually loosen grains from the sandstone. That is why old sandstone buildings often need repairing.
79348.m: Wind and rain make sandstone crumble.

79349.e: Depending on what is between the grains of sand, sandstone can be yellow, red, brown or grey. Red sandstone contains iron, for example.

79350.q: What did sandstone form from a very long time ago?
a: From sand on beaches, in rivers or deserts
79350.e: Sand settled in thick layers on beaches, in rivers or in deserts. Under pressure it slowly turned into solid stone.
79350.m: Sandstone formed from layers of sand.

79351.q: Which stone did marble form from?
79351.e: Marble forms when limestone deep inside the Earth is strongly heated and squeezed. This changes the stone.

79352.q: What is white marble especially famous for?
79352.e: White marble can be carved finely and has a lovely shine. That is why artists have made famous statues from it.
79352.m: Statues are made from white marble.

79353.q: Which country does the famous Carrara marble come from?
79353.e: Carrara is a town in Italy. White marble has been quarried there for over 2000 years.

79354.q: What stone is Michelangelo's famous statue “David” made of?
79354.e: Michelangelo carved “David” from a large block of white marble. The statue stands in Florence.

79355.q: Which famous building in India is built of white marble?
79355.e: The Taj Mahal in Agra is a tomb covered in white marble. The other buildings are made of red or pink sandstone.
79355.m: The Taj Mahal is made of white marble.

79356.q: Which little toy balls get their name from marble?
79356.e: In the past, these little balls were often made of marble. That is why they are called marbles.
79356.m: Marbles get their name from marble.

79357.e: Polished marble has a very smooth surface. It feels cool even on warm days.
79357.m: Polished marble is smooth and cool.

79358.q: How can you often recognise marble?
a: By its holes like in cheese
79358.e: Many kinds of marble have fine, coloured lines. These lines are called veins.

79359.q: What does a rock crystal look like?
79359.e: A rock crystal is colourless and see-through. It looks like clear glass or ice.
79359.m: A rock crystal is clear like glass.

79360.q: How many sides does a rock crystal have all the way round?
79360.e: A rock crystal is a column with six side faces. At the top it comes to a point.
79360.m: A rock crystal has six sides.

79361.q: What are people called in Switzerland who search the mountains for crystals?
79361.e: In Switzerland, crystal hunters are called Strahler. They climb around the Alps looking for crystals.
79361.m: In Switzerland, crystal hunters are called Strahler.

79362.q: Where in Switzerland can you find rock crystals?
a: In fields on the Central Plateau
79362.e: Rock crystals are found mainly in the Alps. The areas around the Grimsel and the Gotthard are especially well known.
79362.m: Rock crystals are found in the Swiss Alps.

79363.q: What did people long ago think a rock crystal was?
79363.e: In the past, many people believed rock crystal was ice that never melts. The word crystal comes from the Greek word for ice.
79363.m: People used to think rock crystal was everlasting ice.

79364.q: Which mineral family does rock crystal belong to?
79364.e: Rock crystal is a very pure, clear form of quartz. Quartz is one of the most common minerals.

79365.q: What shape is the top end of a rock crystal?
79365.e: A rock crystal grows as a six-sided column. Its top end comes together in a point.
79365.m: A rock crystal has a point.

79366.e: Rock crystals grow in cracks and hollows in the rock. Over a long time, quartz from the water builds up there.
79366.m: Rock crystals grow in hollows in the rock.

79367.q: How long do large rock crystals take to grow?
79367.e: Rock crystals grow very slowly. Large crystals need a great many years.

79368.e: The ruby is a red gemstone. Its name comes from the Latin word for red.

79369.e: The emerald is a bright green gemstone. It is one of the most valuable gemstones.

79370.q: What colour is a sapphire usually?
79370.e: Most sapphires are blue. But there are also sapphires in other colours.

79371.e: The amethyst is a purple gemstone. It is a form of quartz.

79372.e: Gemstones are rare, beautiful and hard. That is why they are very precious.
79372.m: Gemstones are rare and therefore valuable.

79373.q: What do people do to gemstones to make them sparkle?
79373.e: Gemstones are cut into shape. Their many smooth faces make them sparkle in the light.

79374.q: What are gemstones often used for?
79374.e: Gemstones are beautiful and rare. That is why they are often set in rings, necklaces and crowns.
79374.m: Gemstones are often used for jewellery.

79375.q: Which of a queen's treasures is often set with lots of gemstones?
79375.e: The crowns of queens and kings are often decorated with gemstones. They show power and wealth.
79375.m: Crowns are often set with gemstones.

79376.q: Which stone is the hardest in nature?
79376.e: Diamond is the hardest natural material. It can scratch almost every other substance.
79376.m: Diamond is the hardest stone in nature.

79377.q: What is a diamond made of?
79377.e: A diamond is made only of carbon. That is the same substance that coal is mostly made of.
79377.m: A diamond is made of carbon.

79378.q: What is the unit used for the weight of diamonds?
79378.e: The weight of diamonds and gemstones is measured in carats. One carat is 0.2 grams.

79379.q: Apart from jewellery, what are diamonds used for?
79379.e: Because diamonds are so hard, they are put into drills and saws. With them you can even cut hard stone.
79379.m: Diamonds help with cutting and drilling.

79380.q: What colour is a typical diamond?
79380.e: Most diamonds in jewellery are colourless and clear. But there are also rare coloured diamonds.

79381.q: What is a cut diamond in jewellery often called?
79381.e: A diamond with a special round cut is called a brilliant. This makes it sparkle especially strongly.
79381.m: A cut diamond is often called a brilliant.

79382.q: What can happen if you hit a diamond hard with a hammer?
79382.e: A diamond is very hard, but it is also brittle. A hard blow can therefore split or shatter it.
79382.m: A diamond is hard, but it can shatter if hit.

79383.e: Diamond is harder than glass. That is why you can scratch and cut glass with it.

79384.q: What do you use to pan for gold in the sand of a stream?
79384.e: You put sand and water into a flat pan and swirl it. The light bits are washed away and the heavy gold stays behind.
79384.m: You pan for gold with a gold pan.

79385.q: Why does gold stay at the bottom of the pan when panning?
79385.e: Gold is much heavier than sand and gravel. That is why it sinks to the bottom when you swirl the pan.
79385.m: Gold stays behind because it is heavy.

79386.q: What does gold that you find in a stream look like?
79386.e: In a stream you usually only find tiny flakes of gold. Big lumps of gold are very rare.
79386.m: In a stream you usually find tiny flakes of gold.

79387.q: Can you find gold in Swiss streams?
79387.e: In some streams, for example in the Napf area, the water carries tiny grains of gold. You hardly ever find big pieces.
79387.m: There are tiny grains of gold in some Swiss streams.

79388.q: What happens to gold if it lies in water for a long time?
79388.e: Gold does not rust and does not change in water. That is why it still shines even after a long time.

79389.q: What is a lump of gold found in nature called?
79389.e: A natural lump of gold is called a nugget. Bars and coins are made by people.
79389.m: A lump of gold from nature is called a nugget.

79390.q: What gets washed out of the pan when panning for gold?
79390.e: When you swirl the pan, the water washes out the lighter grains of sand and little stones. The heavy gold is left behind.
79390.m: When panning for gold, you wash the sand away.

79391.q: What is the time called when, from 1848, huge numbers of people moved to California to find gold?
79391.e: From 1848, thousands of people travelled to California to find gold. This time is called the Gold Rush.
79391.m: In the Gold Rush, lots of people searched for gold.

79392.e: Sand is made of small grains of rock. They have been worn off bigger stones by wind and water.
79392.m: Sand is made of tiny grains of rock.

79393.q: Which sand is better for building a sandcastle?
79393.e: Wet sand sticks together because the water holds the grains together. Dry sand trickles apart.
79393.m: You build sandcastles with wet sand.

79394.q: What is the largest hot desert on Earth, where there is lots of sand?
79394.e: The Sahara in Africa is the largest hot desert in the world. Part of it is covered with huge sand dunes.
79394.m: The Sahara is the largest hot desert.

79395.e: Sand is heated very strongly until it melts. This makes glass for windows and bottles.

79396.e: In an hourglass, sand trickles from the top to the bottom. When it has all run through, a certain amount of time has passed.

79397.q: What are the hills of sand called that the wind piles up in the desert?
79397.e: The wind blows the sand together into big hills. These hills are called dunes.
79397.m: Hills of sand in the desert are called dunes.

79398.q: What do you get if you mix sand, gravel, cement and water?
79398.e: Sand, gravel, cement and water together make concrete. When it dries it becomes rock hard, and houses and bridges are built with it.
79398.m: Concrete is made from sand, gravel, cement and water.

79399.q: What happens to water that you pour onto sand?
79399.e: There are lots of small gaps between the grains of sand. That is why water flows through sand quickly.
79399.m: Water soaks away quickly in sand.

79400.q: How does wet clay soil feel?
79400.e: Wet clay soil is soft and sticky and can be shaped. That is why it sticks to shoes and hands.
79400.m: Wet clay soil is sticky and soft.

79401.q: What happens to clay soil when it dries?
79401.e: When the water evaporates from the clay soil, it becomes firm and hard. It often cracks as it dries.

79402.q: What is made from clay that is fired in a kiln?
79402.e: Bricks are shaped from clay. They are fired in a hot kiln, which makes them very solid.
79402.m: Bricks are made from fired clay.

79403.q: Which bird builds its nest out of little lumps of mud?
79403.e: Swallows collect damp mud in their beaks. They use it to stick their nests onto house walls or inside barns.
79403.m: Swallows build their nests from mud.

79404.q: What can you shape out of clay?
79404.e: Clay is easy to shape. After firing, it becomes solid pots, bowls and jugs.
79404.m: You can shape pots out of clay.

79405.q: What have people in many countries built houses from, in the past and today?
79405.e: Clay soil can be found almost everywhere and it is cheap. That is why people in many countries build houses out of mud bricks.
79405.m: Many houses around the world are built of clay.

79406.q: Why does a puddle often stay on clay soil after rain?
a: Clay soaks up water straight away
79406.e: Clay has very fine grains that lie close together. That is why water only soaks into it slowly.

79407.q: What colour is clay soil often?
79407.e: Clay soil often contains iron. That is why it is usually brown, yellowish or reddish.
79407.m: Clay soil is usually brown or yellowish.

a: Remains of living things that turned to stone
A stone that has been painted
79408.e: A petrification shows remains or prints of living things from long ago. Over a very long time they turned to stone.
79408.m: A petrification is a living thing that turned to stone.

79409.q: What is another word for a living thing that has turned to stone?
79409.e: Remains of living things that have turned to stone are called fossils. A single piece is called a fossil.
79409.m: A living thing turned to stone is called a fossil.

79410.q: What does a fossil ammonite look like?
a: Like a snail shell with a spiral
79410.e: Ammonites were sea creatures with a spiral shell. Their fossils look like coiled snail shells.
79410.m: An ammonite looks like a spiral shell.

79411.q: How long does it take for a living thing to turn to stone?
79411.e: A fossil forms slowly over many thousands to millions of years. The living thing gets covered by layers of sand or mud.
79411.m: A fossil takes a very, very long time to form.

79412.q: What did dinosaurs leave behind that was found in the canton of Jura?
79412.e: In the canton of Jura there are thousands of fossil dinosaur footprints. They show where the animals walked long ago.
79412.m: There are fossil dinosaur tracks in the Jura.

79413.q: What are scientists who study fossils called?
79413.e: Palaeontologists study fossils. This is how they learn which animals and plants lived long ago. Archaeologists, on the other hand, study traces left by people.

79414.q: In which yellow resin stone do you sometimes find trapped insects?
79414.e: Amber is fossilised tree resin. Sometimes it contains trapped insects that lived millions of years ago.
79414.m: You sometimes find insects in amber.

79415.q: Why do people find fossil shells on Swiss mountains?
a: There used to be sea there
79415.e: A very long time ago there was a sea where Switzerland is today. Later the seabed was folded up into mountains.
79415.m: Where there are mountains today, there used to be sea.

79416.q: What does baking powder do in cake mixture?
a: It makes the mixture rock hard
79416.e: Baking powder forms lots of tiny gas bubbles in the mixture. These make the cake light and tall.
79416.m: Baking powder makes the mixture rise.

79417.q: Which gas is produced when baking powder works in dough?
79417.e: Baking powder releases the gas carbon dioxide. The gas bubbles puff up the dough.
79417.m: Baking powder makes the gas carbon dioxide.

79418.q: What is a sponge cake like if you forget the baking powder?
79418.e: Without baking powder, hardly any gas bubbles form in the mixture. The cake does not rise and stays flat and dense.
79418.m: Without baking powder, the cake stays flat.

79419.q: Where does baking powder work best?
79419.e: Baking powder needs moisture and, above all, heat. In a hot oven it makes the most gas.
79419.m: Baking powder works mainly in a hot oven.

79420.e: Baking powder is a fine white powder. That is why you can hardly see it in the mixture.
79420.m: Baking powder is a white powder.

79421.q: Which substance is the most important part of baking powder?
79421.e: Bicarbonate of soda forms gas bubbles in moist, warm dough. That is why it is the most important part of baking powder.
79421.m: Baking powder is mainly bicarbonate of soda.

79422.q: Why does a cake made with baking powder have lots of little holes inside?
79422.e: During baking, lots of gas bubbles form in the mixture. The cake sets and the holes stay.
79422.m: The holes in a cake come from gas bubbles.

79423.q: Which bake is usually made with baking powder?
79423.e: Cakes such as marble cake rise with baking powder. Pizza and bread are usually made with yeast.
79423.m: Marble cake is made with baking powder.

79424.e: Yeast is made of tiny living fungi. You can only see the single yeast cells under a microscope.
79424.m: Yeast is made of tiny living fungi.

79425.q: What do the yeast fungi in dough like to eat most?
79425.e: Yeast fungi feed on sugar. As they do, they make gas that puffs up the dough.

79426.q: What makes a yeast dough rise?
79426.e: The yeast fungi make lots of gas bubbles in the dough. This gas makes the dough big and airy.
79426.m: Yeast makes the dough rise with gas.

79427.q: Where does a yeast dough rise fastest?
79427.e: Yeast likes it warm. In a warm place the yeast fungi work quickly, in the cold only slowly.
79427.m: Yeast dough rises quickly in the warmth.

79428.q: What happens to yeast when it gets very hot?
79428.e: Yeast is made of living things. In great heat they die, for example in the hot oven during baking.

79429.q: Which Swiss Sunday bake is made with yeast?
79429.e: Zopf, a plaited loaf, is made with yeast. The yeast makes it nice and soft and airy.

79430.q: What do you call the process in which yeast makes gas and a little alcohol?
79430.e: This process is called fermentation. The gas makes the dough rise, and the alcohol evaporates during baking.

79431.q: In what form do you often buy fresh yeast in the shop?
79431.e: Fresh yeast is usually sold as a small cube. Dried yeast comes as a powder in a sachet.
79431.m: Fresh yeast is bought as a cube.

79432.e: Vinegar contains an acid. That is why it tastes sour.

79433.q: What is vinegar often used for in the kitchen?
79433.e: Vinegar gives salad dressing a sour taste. It is usually mixed with oil and spices.
79433.m: Vinegar is used for salad dressing.

79434.e: The acetic acid evaporates easily and stings the nose. That is why vinegar smells sharp and sour.

79435.q: What can you remove from a kettle with vinegar?
79435.e: The acid in vinegar dissolves limescale. That is why diluted vinegar helps against white limescale rings.

79436.q: What is cider vinegar made from?
79436.e: Cider vinegar is made from apple juice or cider. This slowly turns sour.
79436.m: Cider vinegar is made from apples.

79437.q: Which tiny living things turn wine into vinegar?
79437.e: Acetic acid bacteria turn the alcohol in wine into acetic acid. This is how wine vinegar is made.

79438.q: Why are gherkins pickled in vinegar?
a: So they go soft like mush
79438.e: The acid in vinegar stops many germs. So pickled gherkins stay good to eat for a long time.

79439.q: What happens to the shell of a raw egg that lies in vinegar for days?
79439.e: The acid in vinegar attacks the hard shell. After a few days only the thin skin is left, and the egg is soft like a rubber ball.

79440.q: What do you often get after eating something very salty?
79440.e: The body has to balance a lot of salt in food with water. That is why you are often very thirsty after salty food.

79441.q: Where does most of the salt in Switzerland come from?
79441.e: Deep underground in Switzerland there are ancient layers of salt. The salt is dissolved out with water, and then the water is evaporated.

79442.q: In which place in the canton of Vaud can you visit an old salt mine?
79442.e: Salt has been mined in Bex for centuries. Visitors can ride into the mine on a little train.
79442.m: There is a salt mine in Bex.

79443.q: Why do you add a pinch of salt to the water for cooking pasta?
79443.e: The pasta takes up a little salt while cooking. That makes it taste more flavourful.
79443.m: Salt in the cooking water gives pasta flavour.

79444.q: What do grains of salt look like under a magnifying glass?
79444.e: Table salt forms cube-shaped crystals. With a magnifying glass you can see the little cubes well.
79444.m: Grains of salt are little cubes.

79445.q: Why is salt spread on icy roads in winter?
79445.e: Salt makes ice melt even in the cold. This makes roads and pavements less slippery.

79446.q: Which substance is added to table salt in Switzerland to keep the thyroid healthy?
79446.e: The body needs iodine for the thyroid gland. That is why Switzerland has had iodised table salt for over 100 years.

79447.q: What do you knead salt dough for crafts from?
79447.e: Salt dough is kneaded from flour, salt and water. After drying or baking it goes hard, and you can paint it.
79447.m: Salt dough is made from flour, salt and water.

79448.q: Which plant is sugar made from in Switzerland?
79448.e: In Switzerland, sugar beet grows in many fields. Sugar is made from its juice.
79448.m: Swiss sugar comes from sugar beet.

79449.q: In which place in the canton of Bern is there a large Swiss sugar factory?
79449.e: Sugar has been made in Aarberg for over 100 years. A second sugar factory is in Frauenfeld.
79449.m: There is a sugar factory in Aarberg.

79450.q: What happens if you stir a lot of sugar into a small glass of water?
79450.e: Water can only dissolve a certain amount of sugar. Anything extra stays at the bottom as grains.
79450.m: Water cannot dissolve endless amounts of sugar.

79451.q: Which plant is much sugar made from in warm countries?
79451.e: Sugar cane is a tall grass that grows in warm countries. Its stalks are full of sweet juice.
79451.m: In warm countries, sugar is made from sugar cane.

79452.q: Which sugar is as fine as flour?
79452.e: Icing sugar is very finely ground sugar. It is used for dusting or for icing.
79452.m: Icing sugar is as fine as flour.

79453.q: What can lots of sweets cause in your teeth?
79453.e: Bacteria in the mouth turn sugar into acid. This acid can attack the teeth and cause tooth decay.
79453.m: Too much sugar can cause tooth decay.

79454.q: What is sugar pressed into little blocks called?
79454.e: Sugar cubes are made of pressed sugar crystals. This makes them easy to count.

79455.e: Green leaves make sugar with sunlight, water and air. The plant stores it, for example, in fruits or roots.
79455.m: Plants make sugar in their green leaves.

79456.q: What do you get when a machine spins melted sugar into fine threads?
79456.e: The machine melts sugar and spins it through tiny holes. The threads set at once and form a cloud.
79456.m: Candyfloss is made of fine sugar threads.

79457.q: What do you sprinkle on crème brûlée before browning it with a flame?
79457.e: Under the hot flame, the sugar melts and turns brown. This makes a crunchy crust on top.
79457.m: Sugar is sprinkled on crème brûlée.

79458.q: What is melted brown sugar called?
79458.e: When sugar is heated strongly, it melts and turns brown. This is called caramel.
79458.m: Brown, melted sugar is called caramel.

79459.q: What does sugar smell like when it caramelises?
79459.e: When sugar caramelises, new scents are formed. That is why it smells sweet and slightly toasted.

79460.q: What happens if you heat caramel for far too long?
79460.e: Sugar heated for too long burns. Then it turns black and tastes bitter.
79460.m: Caramel that gets too hot burns and turns bitter.

79461.q: Why is liquid caramel in the pan dangerous?
a: It is hotter than boiling water
79461.e: Caramel only forms well above 100 degrees. It sticks to the skin and burns it badly.

79462.q: Which Swiss dessert has a caramel sauce?
79462.e: Caramelköpfli is a pudding with a brown caramel sauce. You turn it out onto a plate.

79463.q: What happens to liquid caramel when it cools down?
79463.e: As it cools, liquid caramel sets and becomes as hard as glass. This is how hard sweets are made.

79464.q: Which fairground treat has a coating of caramel?
79464.e: Caramelised almonds are heated with sugar in a pan. The sugar caramelises and coats the almonds.
79464.m: Caramelised almonds have a caramel coating.

79465.q: Which Swiss sweet is made by boiling sugar and cream until it is light brown?
79465.e: For Rahmtäfeli, sugar is boiled with cream and butter. The sugar caramelises and turns the mixture brown.
79465.m: Rahmtäfeli are made from sugar and cream.

79466.q: Why does a cut apple with lemon juice turn brown more slowly?
a: The juice slows down the browning
79466.e: In the air, the flesh of the fruit turns brown. Lemon juice slows this change down.
79466.m: Lemon juice keeps apples pale for longer.

79467.q: Which vitamin is lemon juice especially rich in?
79467.e: Lemons are rich in vitamin C. The body needs it, for example, to fight off illness.
79467.m: Lemons contain a lot of vitamin C.

79468.q: What happens when you pour lemon juice into milk?
79468.e: The acid in the lemon makes the protein in the milk clump together. White flakes form.

79469.q: What happens to a dark, tarnished copper coin when you rub it with lemon juice and salt?
79469.e: The acid in lemon juice dissolves the dark layer on the coin. The shiny metal underneath appears again.
79469.m: Lemon juice makes dark copper shiny again.

79470.q: Where in a lemon is the strong-smelling oil?
79470.e: The lemon peel contains tiny oil glands. If you grate the peel, it smells strongly of lemon.
79470.m: The scented oil is in the lemon peel.

79471.q: What can you produce with a lemon, a piece of copper and a piece of zinc?
79471.e: The sour juice and the two metals together form a simple battery. It supplies a tiny bit of electricity.
79471.m: You can build a battery with a lemon.

79472.q: Which group of fruits does the lemon belong to?
79472.e: The lemon belongs to the citrus fruits. Oranges and mandarins are citrus fruits too.
79472.m: The lemon is a citrus fruit.

79473.q: What happens when you drip lemon juice onto a piece of limestone?
a: The stone goes soft like wax
79473.e: The acid in lemon juice attacks the limestone. This produces a gas that forms little bubbles.

79474.q: What happens when you pour sherbet powder into water?
79474.e: In water, the substances in the sherbet powder react with each other. This forms lots of gas bubbles.

79475.q: Which two substances in sherbet powder fizz together?
a: Bicarbonate of soda and an acid
79475.e: Sherbet powder contains bicarbonate of soda and an acid. Together with water they make gas.
79475.m: Bicarbonate of soda and acid make sherbet powder fizz.

79476.q: Which acid is often found in sherbet powder?
79476.e: Sherbet powder usually contains citric acid or tartaric acid. It also gives the slightly sour taste.
79476.m: Sherbet powder often contains citric acid.

79477.q: What do you feel when you sprinkle sherbet powder on your tongue?
79477.e: Saliva is moist. That is why the sherbet powder starts to fizz and tingle on your tongue.
79477.m: Sherbet powder tingles on the tongue.

79478.q: Why must sherbet powder be kept dry?
a: Otherwise it fizzes in the tin
79478.e: Moisture starts the reaction. Then the powder is used up before you put it in the glass.

79479.q: What is a pressed tablet that fizzes in water called?
79479.e: An effervescent tablet contains the same substances as sherbet powder. It is just pressed tightly together.

79480.e: Besides bicarbonate of soda and acid, sherbet powder contains sugar. It gives the sweet taste.

79481.q: Where does sherbet powder fizz faster, in warm or in cold water?
79481.e: In warm water, chemical reactions happen faster. That is why sherbet powder fizzes more strongly there and is finished sooner.
79481.m: Sherbet powder fizzes faster in warm water.

79482.e: Lactic acid bacteria eat the milk sugar. As they do, they make acid, and the milk goes sour.

79483.q: Which acid forms in soured milk?
79483.e: The bacteria turn the milk sugar into lactic acid. This acid gets its name from milk (Latin ‘lac’).
79483.m: Lactic acid forms in soured milk.

79484.q: How does milk change when it goes sour?
79484.e: The acid makes the protein in the milk curdle. That is why soured milk gets thicker.

79485.q: Which dairy product is made with the help of lactic acid bacteria?
79485.e: To make yoghurt, lactic acid bacteria are added to warm milk. They make the milk sour and thick.
79485.m: Yoghurt is made with lactic acid bacteria.

79486.q: Where does milk go sour fastest?
79486.e: Bacteria multiply quickly in the warmth. In the fridge they work only slowly.
79486.m: Milk goes sour quickly in the warmth.

79487.q: What does soured milk taste like?
79487.e: Soured milk contains lactic acid. That is why it tastes slightly sour.

79488.q: What do you get when you let soured, thick milk drain?
79488.e: As it drains, the liquid runs away. A thick, white mass is left behind: quark.
79488.m: Quark is made from soured milk.

79489.q: What is the yellowish liquid that separates from soured milk called?
79489.e: When milk curdles, a yellowish liquid separates off. This liquid is called whey.
79489.m: The liquid from curdled milk is called whey.

79490.q: What happens to egg white when it is cooked?
79490.e: Raw egg white is see-through and runny. The heat makes it white and firm.
79490.m: Cooked egg white turns white and firm.

79491.q: About how long do you boil a hard-boiled egg?
79491.e: A medium egg is hard after about 10 minutes in boiling water. A soft-boiled egg needs only about 5 minutes.
79491.m: A hard-boiled egg boils for about 10 minutes.

79492.q: Can you make a boiled egg raw again?
79492.e: When cooked, the egg white changes for ever. This change cannot be undone.
79492.m: A boiled egg never becomes raw again.

79493.q: How does a hard-boiled egg spin on the table?
79493.e: Everything inside a hard-boiled egg is solid, so it spins like a top. A raw egg wobbles because the inside sloshes about.
79493.m: A hard-boiled egg spins like a top.

79494.q: Why do you put eggs in cold water after boiling them?
a: So they take in more salt
79494.e: A hot egg keeps cooking even outside the pan. Cold water cools it down quickly.

79495.q: What does the yolk get if you boil an egg for far too long?
79495.e: If boiled too long, substances from the white and the yolk react with each other. This produces a greenish rim.
79495.m: Eggs boiled too long have a green rim.

79496.q: Why are eggs often pricked before boiling?
79496.e: There is a small air bubble inside an egg. Through the hole, the air can escape when heated, and the shell cracks less often.

79497.q: Which sets first when cooking, the egg white or the yolk?
79497.e: The egg white is on the outside and gets hot first. It also sets at a slightly lower temperature than the yolk.
79497.m: When cooking, the egg white sets first.

79498.q: Which cereal is popcorn made from?
79498.e: Popcorn is made from a special kind of maize. The kernels burst open when heated.

79499.q: What is inside a maize kernel that turns to steam when heated?
79499.e: Inside the kernel there is some water. When heated, it turns into hot steam.
79499.m: A maize kernel contains a little water.

79500.q: Why does a maize kernel burst open when heated?
a: The kernel is cut from the outside
The oil presses from the outside
79500.e: The steam inside the kernel presses harder and harder against the hard shell. At some point it suddenly splits open.
79500.m: Steam bursts the maize kernel open.

79501.q: What is the kind of maize used to make popcorn called?
79501.e: Popping corn has an especially hard shell. That is why enough pressure can build up inside.
79501.m: Popcorn is made from popping corn.

79502.q: Why does a maize kernel with a crack in its shell not pop properly?
79502.e: The steam can slowly escape through the crack. So no pressure builds up to burst the kernel.
79502.m: A kernel with a crack does not pop properly.

79503.q: What do you hear when popcorn pops in the pan?
79503.e: Each kernel bursts open with a small bang. That is why the pan keeps popping.
79503.m: Popcorn pops as it bursts open.

79504.q: How does a maize kernel change when it becomes popcorn?
79504.e: When it bursts, the soft inside of the kernel puffs up. The popcorn is much bigger than the kernel was before.
79504.m: Popcorn is much bigger than the maize kernel.

79505.q: Where does maize originally come from?
79505.e: Maize was first grown in Central America. Only later did it come to Europe.

79506.q: Why do you put a lid on the pan when making popcorn?
a: So the kernels don't jump out
79506.e: The bursting kernels jump up. With the lid they stay in the pan, and hot oil does not spatter out.
79506.m: A lid keeps the popcorn in the pan.

79507.q: Which parts of the sunflower is sunflower oil pressed from?
79507.e: Sunflower seeds contain a lot of oil. It is pressed out in an oil mill.
79507.m: Sunflower oil comes from the seeds.

79508.q: Which yellow-flowering field crop is most home-grown cooking oil in Switzerland pressed from?
79508.e: In spring, many rapeseed fields bloom yellow in Switzerland. Rapeseed oil is pressed from the small seeds.
79508.m: A lot of rapeseed oil is made in Switzerland.

79509.q: Which oil is made from the fruit of trees around the Mediterranean?
79509.e: Olive trees grow mainly around the Mediterranean. Olive oil is pressed from their fruit.

79510.q: What does a drop of oil leave on paper?
79510.e: Oil soaks into the paper and does not evaporate like water. That is why a see-through grease spot is left.
79510.m: Oil leaves a grease spot on paper.

79511.q: Why is cooking oil best kept in a dark, cool place?
79511.e: Light, warmth and air change the oil over time. Then it smells and tastes rancid.
79511.m: Keep cooking oil dark and cool.

79512.q: What does oil feel like between your fingers?
79512.e: Oil makes the skin smooth and slippery. That is why it feels slippery.

79513.q: Where should old cooking oil go?
79513.e: Oil blocks pipes and pollutes water. That is why you take it to a collection point in a bottle.
79513.m: Old oil goes to a collection point.

79514.q: What often happens to olive oil in the fridge?
79514.e: In the cold, some fats in olive oil go solid. That is why it goes cloudy and thick, but clear again when warm.
79514.m: Olive oil goes cloudy in the cold.

79515.e: Chips are deep-fried in hot oil. The oil is much hotter than boiling water and makes them crispy.
79515.m: Chips are fried in hot oil.

a: A place where water comes out of the ground
A lake high up in the mountains
A place where a river ends
80310.e: At a spring, water comes out of the ground or out of a rock into the daylight. A stream often starts there.
80310.m: At a spring, water comes out of the earth.

80311.q: Why is spring water often cool even in summer?
a: It comes from the cool ground
It flows over blocks of ice
It falls from the sky at night
80311.e: Deep in the ground it stays about equally cool all year. That is why spring water is pleasantly fresh even on hot days.
80311.m: Spring water comes up cool from deep down.

80312.q: What is a spring called that warm water comes out of?
80312.e: The water of a thermal spring is heated deep inside the Earth. In Switzerland there are such springs in Baden or Leukerbad, for example.
80312.m: Warm water bubbles out of a thermal spring.

80313.q: What is a hot spring called that shoots water high into the air again and again?
80313.e: In a geyser, water underground gets so hot that it shoots upwards with steam. There are famous geysers in Iceland.
80313.m: A geyser shoots hot water into the air.

80314.q: Where does the water of the Rhône come from right at the start?
80314.e: The Rhône begins with meltwater from the Rhône Glacier in the canton of Valais.
80314.m: The Rhône begins at the Rhône Glacier in Valais.

80315.q: What is spring water with lots of dissolved minerals called that you can buy in bottles?
80315.e: On its way through the rock, water picks up minerals. Spring water like this is bottled and sold as mineral water.
80315.m: Mineral water comes from a spring.

80316.q: Can a spring dry up in summer?
a: Yes, if it does not rain for a long time
80316.e: A spring is fed by rain and snow that soak into the ground. If there is no rain for a long time, it can give less water or dry up completely.
80316.m: Without rain a spring can dry up.

80317.q: Where is the source of a river?
80317.e: A river begins at its source and then flows downhill. At the end it flows into another river, a lake or the sea.
80317.m: A river begins at its source.

a: A small body of flowing water
80318.e: A stream is smaller and narrower than a river. Its water keeps on flowing.
80318.m: A stream is a small body of flowing water.

80319.q: What forms when lots of streams flow together?
80319.e: Streams join together and get bigger and bigger. This is how a river forms.
80319.m: Lots of streams make a river.

80320.q: Which fish likes living in cool, clean streams?
80320.e: The brown trout needs cool water with lots of oxygen. It lives in many Swiss streams. Carp and catfish prefer warm, calm water.
80320.m: The trout likes cool, clean water.

80321.q: Which little creature under the stones in a stream shows that the water is clean?
80321.e: Freshwater shrimps need clean water with lots of oxygen. If you find lots of them, the stream is healthy.
80321.m: Lots of freshwater shrimps show the water is clean.

80322.q: Which bird dives in streams for small creatures?
80322.e: The dipper is a small songbird. It dives and even walks underwater along the bed of the stream.
80322.m: The dipper dives in streams for food.

80323.q: Which way does a stream flow?
80323.e: Because of gravity, water always flows downwards. That is why a stream flows downhill.

80324.q: Why does a mountain stream often flow very fast?
80324.e: The steeper the ground, the faster the water flows. In the mountains it is often very steep.
80324.m: The steeper the slope, the faster the stream.

80325.q: Which plant with yellow flowers likes to grow on wet stream banks in spring?
80325.e: The marsh marigold loves wet ground by streams and ditches. In spring its yellow flowers shine.
80325.m: The marsh marigold flowers yellow on stream banks.

80326.q: What does a beaver build in a stream?
80326.e: The beaver blocks the stream with branches and mud. This makes a pond where it can build its lodge safely.

a: Water that plunges over a rock step
Water that comes out of the ground
80327.e: In a waterfall, a stream or river flows over a steep step and falls down.
80327.m: A waterfall plunges down over a rock step.

80328.q: What can you often see in the fine spray of a waterfall when the sun is shining?
80328.e: The sun shines into the many tiny drops of water. These split the light into its colours.
80328.m: A rainbow often appears in the spray of a waterfall.

80329.q: What are the famous waterfalls between Canada and the USA called?
80329.e: Niagara Falls lie on the border between Canada and the USA. Millions of people visit them every year.
80329.m: Niagara Falls lie between Canada and the USA.

80330.q: What is the highest waterfall in the world called?
80330.e: Angel Falls is in Venezuela in South America. Its water falls almost 1000 metres.
80330.m: The highest waterfall in the world is Angel Falls.

80331.q: Which Swiss waterfalls plunge down inside a mountain?
80331.e: The Trümmelbach Falls thunder through a gorge inside the mountain near Lauterbrunnen. A lift takes visitors inside.
80331.m: The Trümmelbach Falls roar inside a mountain.

80332.q: What can the power of falling water be used for?
80332.e: Falling water drives turbines that make electricity. In Switzerland a lot of electricity comes from hydropower.

80333.q: What is it called when people climb up frozen waterfalls in winter?
80333.e: In ice climbing, you climb up frozen waterfalls with ice axes and crampons. You only do this with training and safety ropes.
80333.m: You can go ice climbing on frozen waterfalls.

80334.q: Which village is the Staubbach Falls near?
80334.e: The Staubbach Falls plunge over a cliff into the valley right by the village of Lauterbrunnen.
80334.m: The Staubbach Falls are at Lauterbrunnen.

80335.q: Which canton are the Staubbach Falls in?
80335.e: The Staubbach Falls are in the Bernese Oberland, which is in the canton of Bern.
80335.m: The Staubbach Falls are in the canton of Bern.

80336.q: Roughly how high are the Staubbach Falls?
80336.e: The water of the Staubbach falls about 297 metres. It is one of the highest waterfalls in Switzerland.
80336.m: The Staubbach Falls are almost 300 metres high.

80337.q: Why are the Staubbach Falls called that? (“Staub” means dust in German.)
a: The water breaks up into fine droplets
They bring lots of dust into the valley
80337.e: On its long way down, the wind scatters the water in all directions. It then looks like fine dust.
80337.m: At the Staubbach Falls, the water turns into spray like dust.

80338.q: Which famous poet wrote a poem at the Staubbach Falls in 1779?
80338.e: Goethe visited the Staubbach Falls on a journey through Switzerland. There he wrote the poem “Song of the Spirits over the Waters”.
80338.m: Goethe wrote a poem at the Staubbach Falls.

80339.q: How can you get close to the Staubbach Falls in summer?
a: Through a gallery in the rock
By a lift in a tower
80339.e: In summer a path leads to a rock gallery at the Staubbach Falls. At other times the path is closed because of falling ice and rocks.
80339.m: In summer a path leads up to the Staubbach Falls.

80340.q: How does the water fall at the Staubbach Falls?
80340.e: The water plunges almost freely from the edge of the cliff. On the way down it turns into fine spray.
80340.m: The Staubbach falls freely over a cliff.

80341.q: When does the Staubbach carry the most water?
a: In early summer when the snow melts
80341.e: When the snow in the mountains melts in early summer, especially large amounts of water flow into the streams. In winter much of it is frozen.
80341.m: When the snow melts, mountain streams carry lots of water.

80342.q: Where does most of the drinking water in Switzerland come from?
80342.e: About 80 per cent of Swiss drinking water comes from groundwater and springs. The rest comes mainly from lakes.
80342.m: Most of Switzerland's drinking water comes from groundwater.

80343.q: What is used today to bring groundwater up from deep down?
80343.e: Pumps suck the groundwater up through pipes. Then it flows into the water mains.

80344.q: Why is groundwater often very clean?
80344.e: On its way through soil, sand and gravel, lots of bits of dirt get caught. The ground works like a filter.

a: Poison or too much fertiliser in the soil
80345.e: Whatever soaks into the ground can reach the groundwater. That is why you must never pour poison or oil onto the ground.
80345.m: Poison in the soil can pollute groundwater.

80346.q: How did people long ago get water up from a deep well?
a: With a bucket on a rope
80346.e: A well like this reaches down to the groundwater. People lowered a bucket on a rope and pulled it back up full of water.
80346.m: People used to get well water up with a bucket.

80347.q: Where in the ground is groundwater usually found?
a: In gaps between gravel and sand
In big caves full of air
80347.e: Groundwater fills the tiny spaces between small stones, gravel and sand. There is usually no open underground lake.
80347.m: Groundwater is in the gaps between gravel and sand.

a: Yes, as fast as a river
80348.e: Groundwater moves slowly through the ground, often only a few metres a day. It flows towards rivers or lakes.

80349.q: What happens to groundwater if it does not rain for a very long time?
a: It gets as warm as a bath
80349.e: Without rain, no new water comes in. The water table then slowly drops.
80349.m: In a drought, the groundwater sinks.

a: When the ground is completely dry
80350.e: Rainwater flows into small dips in the ground. If it cannot soak away quickly, a puddle is left.
80350.m: Puddles collect in dips after rain.

80351.q: Why do puddles on tarmac stay for a long time?
a: Tarmac does not let water through
80351.e: Tarmac is sealed, so the water cannot soak into the ground. It stays there until it evaporates or drains away.
80351.m: Tarmac does not let rainwater through.

80352.q: Where does a puddle go on a sunny day?
a: A bird drinks it all up
80352.e: The warmth of the sun makes the water evaporate. It becomes invisible water vapour in the air.

80353.q: What shimmers in a puddle when a little oil is floating on it?
80353.e: A very thin layer of oil on the water makes the light shimmer in bright colours.
80353.m: Oil on a puddle shimmers in many colours.

80354.q: What happens to a puddle on a frosty night?
80354.e: Below 0 degrees, water turns into ice. In the morning the puddle is then often covered with a layer of ice.
80354.m: Puddles freeze when there is frost.

80355.q: Which birds collect wet mud from puddles to build their nests?
80355.e: Swallows make little balls out of damp mud. They use them to stick their nests under a roof, for example.
80355.m: Swallows build their nests from mud.

80356.q: What do you see when you look into a still puddle?
80356.e: The smooth surface of the water reflects the light like a mirror. That is why you see yourself and the sky.
80356.m: A still puddle reflects like a mirror.

80357.q: Which insects like to lay their eggs in puddles and water butts?
80357.e: Mosquitoes need still water for their larvae. Even a small puddle can be enough.
80357.m: Mosquitoes lay eggs in still water.

80358.q: Which animals sometimes lay their eggs in puddles in wheel ruts?
80358.e: Some toads, such as the yellow-bellied toad, like small, warm puddles, for example in wheel ruts. They lay their spawn there.
80358.m: Toads also lay their eggs in puddles.

80359.q: On which nights does a lot of dew form?
80359.e: Without clouds, the ground cools down a lot at night. Without wind, the water from the air can then settle easily on the grass.
80359.m: Clear, calm nights bring lots of dew.

80360.q: Where does the water in dewdrops come from?
a: From water vapour in the air
80360.e: There is invisible water vapour in the air. When the air cools down, it turns back into liquid water in small drops.
80360.m: Dew forms from water vapour in the air.

80361.q: What happens to dew when the sun shines in the morning?
a: It turns into fog in the ground
80361.e: The sun warms the grass and the air. The drops then turn back into water vapour.

80362.q: Where do dewdrops glitter especially beautifully in the morning?
80362.e: Lots of little drops hang on the fine threads of a spider's web. In the morning light they glitter like pearls.
80362.m: Dewdrops glitter like pearls on spiders' webs.

80363.q: What happens to cold glasses when you come into a warm room?
a: They steam up with tiny droplets
80363.e: The warm air in the room contains water vapour. On the cold glasses it turns into tiny drops, just like dew.
80363.m: Water droplets form on cold surfaces.

80364.q: On a clear night, when is it usually coolest?
80364.e: The ground cools down all night long. That is why it is usually coldest at sunrise, and there is lots of dew.
80364.m: It is often coolest at sunrise.

80365.q: Why is there often less dew under a tree in the morning?
a: The ground there cools down less
The sun shines there at night
80365.e: The treetop works like a blanket and holds back some warmth. The ground underneath gets less cold, so less dew forms.
80365.m: Under trees it cools down less and there is less dew.

a: Fine ice crystals on branches and grass
80366.e: Hoar frost is made of lots of tiny ice crystals. They grow on trees, fences and grass.
80366.m: Hoar frost is made of fine ice crystals.

80367.q: In what weather does hoar frost form?
a: When it is frosty and the air is damp
When it is hot and sunny
80367.e: Hoar frost forms when it is colder than 0 degrees and the air is damp, for example in fog. The tiny droplets freeze onto everything they touch.
80367.m: Hoar frost needs frost and damp air.

80368.e: The many fine ice crystals scatter the light. That is why hoar frost looks white.

80369.q: In which season do we see hoar frost in Switzerland?
80369.e: Hoar frost needs temperatures below 0 degrees. In Switzerland that happens mainly in winter and on cold autumn nights.
80369.m: You see hoar frost mainly in winter.

80370.q: On which side of the twigs does hoar frost grow most?
a: On the side the wind comes from
On the side facing the ground
80370.e: The wind carries the damp, cold air against the twigs. Where it hits them, the ice crystals grow the most.
80370.m: Hoar frost grows towards the wind.

80371.q: What are the patterns of ice called that grow on cold window panes?
80371.e: On cold panes the moisture freezes into branching patterns. They look like flowers made of ice.
80371.m: Frost flowers are ice patterns on windows.

80372.q: What can happen when a lot of hoar frost hangs on trees?
80372.e: Thick hoar frost can get very heavy. Then the branches bend and some break off.
80372.m: Heavy hoar frost can break branches.

80373.q: What happens to hoar frost when it gets warmer?
80373.e: When the temperature rises above 0 degrees, the ice crystals melt. They often fall off the branches like fine snow, too.
80373.m: Hoar frost melts when it gets warmer.

a: Dripping water freezes bit by bit
80374.e: Water runs down an edge and freezes drop by drop. This makes the icicle longer and longer.

80375.q: Why is it dangerous to walk under big icicles?
80375.e: Big icicles are heavy and pointed. If they come loose, they can hurt people.
80375.m: It is better not to walk under big icicles.

80376.q: In what weather do icicles grow especially well?
a: The sun melts snow, but the air is cold
80376.e: The sun melts some snow on the roof. The water drips down and freezes into ice in the cold air.
80376.m: Icicles grow when melting snow freezes in cold air.

80377.q: Which way do icicles grow on a roof?
80377.e: Because of gravity, the water drips downwards. That is why icicles grow from the top down.

80378.q: What happens to icicles when it thaws?
a: They get as hard as stone
80378.e: When it gets warmer than 0 degrees, the ice melts. The icicles drip and get smaller until they fall off.

80379.q: Why are icicles pointed at the bottom?
a: The least water reaches the bottom
Birds peck them into a point
80379.e: Most of the water freezes further up the icicle. Only a little reaches the tip, so it stays thin.
80379.m: Icicles are thick at the top and pointed at the bottom.

80380.q: Where in nature can very long icicles hang in winter?
80380.e: In winter, water seeps out of cracks in the rocks. It freezes and sometimes forms icicles several metres long.
80380.m: Huge icicles grow on rock faces in winter.

a: A very wet area with soft ground
80381.e: In a bog the ground is full of water and very soft. You can sink into it.
80381.m: A bog is a wet area with soft ground.

80382.q: Which animals like living in a wet bog?
80382.e: In a bog there is lots of water and lots of insects. That is why frogs feel at home there.

80383.q: Why are many bogs in Switzerland protected?
a: Rare plants and animals live there
Lots of vegetables are grown there
The best ski slopes are there
Most of the timber grows there
80383.e: In bogs there are plants and animals that are hardly found anywhere else. That is why many bogs are protected.
80383.m: Bogs are home to rare plants and animals.

80384.q: Which small meat-eating plant grows in Swiss bogs?
80384.e: The sundew has sticky drops on its leaves. Small insects get stuck to them and are digested.
80384.m: The sundew catches insects with sticky drops.

80385.q: Who decided in 1987 that bogs in Switzerland should be specially protected?
80385.e: In the vote on the Rothenthurm initiative, the people said yes to protecting bogs. Since then this has been in the Federal Constitution.
80385.m: The Swiss people decided to protect bogs in 1987.

80386.q: Why can a bog store so much water?
a: The moss soaks up water like a sponge
The ground is made of hard rock
Lots of big trees grow there
80386.e: Peat moss can hold many times its own weight in water. This is how the bog holds on to lots of water.
80386.m: A bog stores water like a sponge.

80387.q: Why should you stay on the paths in a bog?
a: You can sink in and trample plants
It is warmer on the paths
It is too dark beside the paths
80387.e: The soft ground of the bog cannot hold you everywhere. Also, rare plants grow there that are easily damaged.
80387.m: In a bog, you stay on the paths.

80388.q: What colour is the water in a raised bog often?
80388.e: Substances from dead plants dissolve in the water. They turn it brown like tea.
80388.m: Bog water is often brown like tea.

a: A small, shallow body of still water
80389.e: A pond is small and so shallow that plants often grow right down to the bottom. The water hardly flows.
80389.m: A pond is a small, shallow body of water.

80390.q: Which animals lay their spawn in the pond in spring?
80390.e: Frogs lay their eggs in the water as spawn. The clumps of eggs float in the pond.
80390.m: Frogs lay spawn in the pond in spring.

80391.q: What are young frogs called that still live in the water?
80391.e: Tadpoles hatch from frogspawn. They have a tail and breathe with gills until they become frogs.

80392.q: Which insect with shimmering wings hunts mosquitoes over ponds?
80392.e: Dragonflies are fast fliers and catch other insects in the air. Their larvae live in the water.
80392.m: Dragonflies hunt mosquitoes over the water.

80393.q: Which insect can walk on the surface of the water?
80393.e: The pond skater is very light and has long legs with fine hairs. That is why it does not sink.
80393.m: The pond skater walks on water.

80394.q: Which plant with big round leaves floats on ponds?
80394.e: The water lily has its roots in the mud at the bottom. Its leaves and flowers float on the water.
80394.m: The water lily floats on the pond.

80395.q: Which plant on the edge of a pond has brown heads that look like sausages?
80395.e: The bulrush grows in shallow water at the edge. Its brown heads are full of seeds.
80395.m: The bulrush has brown heads at the water's edge.

80396.q: Why does a pond freeze over faster in winter than a big lake?
a: It is always in a forest
80396.e: A small, shallow pond holds little water. It cools down quickly and therefore freezes over sooner than a big, deep lake.
80396.m: Small, shallow ponds freeze over quickly.

80397.q: Which bird often swims on ponds, with the male having a shiny green head?
80397.e: The mallard is the most common duck in Switzerland. You can recognise the male by its shimmering green head.
80397.m: The male mallard has a green head.

80398.q: Why can you not drink seawater?
80398.e: Seawater contains a lot of salt. If you drink it, you get even thirstier, because your body has to get rid of the salt.
80398.m: Seawater is too salty to drink.

80399.q: Is there more sea or more land on Earth?
80399.e: Most of the Earth is covered by sea. That is why the Earth is also called the blue planet.
80399.m: Most of the Earth is covered by sea.

80400.q: Which sea does the Rhine flow into in the end?
80400.e: The Rhine flows from Switzerland through Germany and the Netherlands. There it flows into the North Sea.
80400.m: The Rhine flows into the North Sea.

80401.q: Which sea does the Rhône flow into in the end?
80401.e: The Rhône flows through Lake Geneva and then through France. It flows into the Mediterranean in southern France.
80401.m: The Rhône flows into the Mediterranean.

80402.q: Which sea does the water of the Inn from the Engadine reach?
80402.e: The Inn flows into the Danube. The Danube finally flows into the Black Sea.
80402.m: The water of the Inn reaches the Black Sea.

80403.q: What is the largest animal in the sea?
80403.e: The blue whale can grow over 30 metres long. It is even the largest animal that has ever lived on Earth.
80403.m: The blue whale is the largest animal in the world.

80405.q: What do you do with finely chopped red cabbage to get red cabbage juice?
80405.e: The hot water draws the colour out of the leaves. After cooling, you pour the coloured juice through a sieve.
80405.m: Hot water draws the colour out of red cabbage.

80406.q: What colour is red cabbage juice in pure water?
80406.e: In water that is neither acidic nor basic, red cabbage juice is purple. Only when you add something does the colour change.
80406.m: In pure water, red cabbage juice is purple.

80407.q: What colour does red cabbage juice turn when you stir in bicarbonate of soda?
80407.e: Bicarbonate of soda is not acidic but basic. That is why the purple red cabbage juice turns blue to blue-green.
80407.m: Bicarbonate of soda turns red cabbage juice blue.

80408.q: What does red cabbage juice show with its colour?
80408.e: The dye in red cabbage changes colour depending on whether a substance is acidic or basic. This lets you test things from the kitchen.
80408.m: Red cabbage juice shows by its colour whether something is acidic.

80409.q: What do you call a substance that shows by its colour whether something is acidic?
80409.e: An indicator is something that shows. Red cabbage juice is an indicator you can make yourself.
80409.m: An indicator shows by its colour whether something is acidic.

80410.q: What does a splash of vinegar do to the colour when cooking red cabbage?
80410.e: Acid from vinegar or sour apples keeps red cabbage red. Without acid it tends to turn bluish when cooked.
80410.m: With a little acid, cooked red cabbage stays red.

80411.q: What property does lemon juice have if it turns red cabbage juice red?
80411.e: Lemon juice contains acid. Acidic substances turn red cabbage juice red.
80411.m: Acidic substances turn red cabbage juice red.

80412.q: Which juice, like red cabbage juice, changes colour with acid?
80412.e: Blueberries contain a blue dye similar to red cabbage. That is why their juice also changes colour with acid.
80412.m: Blueberry juice also changes colour with acid.

80413.q: What is food colouring used for?
80413.e: Food colouring is safe to eat. It is used, for example, to colour cakes, icing or Easter eggs.

80414.q: Which colour do you get when you mix red and yellow food colouring?
80414.e: Red and yellow together make orange. This way you can mix many new colours from just a few.
80414.m: Red and yellow together make orange.

80415.q: Which vegetable colours food bright red?
